item.title: Trump DHS chief under fire from conservatives after immigration speech ignites backlash
item.description: Former Border Patrol Chief Gregory Bovino accused Markwayne Mullin of undermining mass deportations after the DHS secretary called for immigration reform.
item.content:encoded:
Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin is facing a conservative backlash after reaffirming his opposition to amnesty in a social media post, with critics arguing the hardline message contradicted comments he made hours earlier during an immigration speech in Oklahoma.

Hours after speaking at the National Governors Association Summer Meeting in Oklahoma City, Mullin wrote on X: "NO amnesty for illegal aliens. Ever."

"We are a nation of laws," he wrote. "If you are illegally present in the United States of America—you will be detained and deported. Period."

The post did little to quell criticism from some conservatives, who argued it conflicted with remarks Mullin made earlier in the day.

RED STATE GOVERNOR PUMMELED ONLINE AFTER DEFYING TRUMP’S DEPORTATION ORDERS

"Why were you at the National Governors Association Summer Meeting today saying the exact opposite of what you are posting now?" one user wrote on X. "Did you suddenly radically change your mind about America's immigration policy in the past couple of hours? Or are you a liar?"

Former Border Patrol Chief Gregory Bovino also criticized Mullin's remarks, writing on X that "Voters asked for mass deportations. Clear demand. High priority. No ambiguity." He added, "The guy running DHS is making the case for 'immigration reform.' We've seen this script before."

In a separate post, Bovino wrote that Mullin had delivered "a masterclass in how to give terrible answers during a single interview" and argued, "Now you know why we're not getting mass deportations."

Conservative commentator Robby Starbuck also weighed in, calling Mullin's remarks "a total betrayal."

During the event, Mullin argued the U.S. needs immigration reform, distinguished between immigrants pursuing legal status and those who are not, and called for changes to some employment visa programs to address labor shortages.

"We haven't had actual immigration reform since 1959. There's a reason. It's political," Mullin said. "Do you really need immigration reform? Yes, you do."

BIDEN ADMINISTRATION FORCED A FALSE CHOICE ON AMERICANS ABOUT IMMIGRATION

Mullin also argued the country should modernize some employment visa programs.

"If we're looking to grow our economy, then we need to look at making more permanent solutions," he said, adding that "there's a way to utilize labor where we're not having the participation rate we need to... and we can plug those holes."

At the same time, Mullin repeatedly emphasized that immigration laws must be enforced.

"If you have a criminal background, we're not making exceptions for you," he said. "There are zero exceptions."

Mullin added that immigrants who entered the country illegally or overstayed their visas without pursuing legal status could not expect relief.

"There's nothing I can do for you," he said.

The Department of Homeland Security did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

item.title: Mayor calls upscale restaurant bombing a 'brutal terrorist act' after 3 killed, 21 injured
item.description: Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin vowed to hunt down those responsible after a body-worn bomb detonated at an upscale restaurant on Saturday killing three.
item.content:encoded:
A bombing at an upscale restaurant in Moscow that killed three people and wounded at least 21 others on Saturday was a "brutal terrorist act," according to the city’s mayor, who vowed to hunt down those responsible for the attack.

Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin made the declaration Sunday, a day after the explosion tore through the Balzi Rossi Italian restaurant in the Russian capital.

"Yesterday, a brutal terrorist act was committed in Moscow that claimed human lives. The victims are currently in the city’s hospitals, where they are receiving all necessary care," Sobyanin wrote on social media Sunday.

EXPLOSION AT RESTAURANT IN CENTRAL MOSCOW LEAVES THREE DEAD, MORE THAN A DOZEN INJURED

He added investigators are working to identify those behind the attack and vowed they "will certainly be found and will face the punishment they deserve."

Russian authorities have not identified any suspects, and no group had claimed responsibility as of Sunday.

Russia's National Anti-Terrorism Committee said the blast was caused by a homemade explosive device. Russian state news agency RIA Novosti, citing local officials, reported that a woman carrying the bomb tried to enter the restaurant but was stopped by a security guard before it exploded.

The blast killed the woman, the security guard and a restaurant patron, RIA Novosti reported. At least 21 other people were injured in the explosion, which happened around 8 p.m. local time at the restaurant on Kudrinskaya Square.

UKRAINE UNLEASHES MORE THAN 400 DRONES NEAR MOSCOW IN ONE OF WAR'S BIGGEST ATTACKS

The restaurant was closed to the public Saturday night for a private event, according to its website and Russian state media.

Video released by Russian state media showed heavily armed police officers, ambulances and other emergency vehicles outside the damaged restaurant as investigators examined the scene.

Earlier this year, Russia's Federal Security Service, or FSB, said it would tighten security for senior military and government officials following a series of assassination attempts in Russian cities since the Kremlin launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

Russian authorities have not linked the restaurant bombing to those earlier attacks or to the war in Ukraine.

Fox News Digital’s Brie Stimson and The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: Bryan Kohberger's former defense expert calls for death penalty, says investigators missed key evidence
item.description: A defense expert hired by Bryan Kohberger now says cell phone data shows evidence of stalking, contradicting his own earlier expert report in the case.
item.content:encoded:
Admitted Idaho murderer Bryan Kohberger should get a new trial and face the death penalty, according to a digital forensics expert hired by the defense who says investigators missed damning evidence against the 30-year-old former criminology PhD student — although his own expert report for the case appears to contradict some of the claims.

Sy Ray is a former Arizona homicide investigator who is now an expert on digital forensics, geolocation and similar data. Kohberger's lawyers hired him as an expert witness for the defense before Kohberger pleaded guilty to avoid the death penalty for the home invasion murders of Kaylee Goncalves, 21, Madison Mogen, 21, Xana Kernodle, 20, and Ethan Chapin, also 20.

Kohberger, now serving four consecutive sentences of life in prison without parole, petitioned the court last week to withdraw his guilty plea and seek post-conviction relief, which could send the case to trial — and put the potential death penalty back in play.

KOHBERGER DEFENSE EXPERT WANTS HIS LAWYERS UNDER OATH AFTER KILLER CITES FINDINGS IN BID TO UNDO GUILTY PLEA

"Bring back the death penalty," Ray told journalist Brian Entin in a new podcast. "I am all for this."

He said he is confident that Kohberger would be convicted and claimed that Kohberger's smartphone data is much more incriminating than was revealed previously when police and the courts unsealed thousands of pages of evidence in the case.

"I 100% believe that the offender, who is Bryan Kohberger — there’s no alternative theory in my head at this point," Ray said in the 82-minute episode, which also included Goncalves’ parents, Kristi and Steve, and her older sister, Alivea. "I 100% believe he’s been in the house before."

BRYAN KOHBERGER'S CHOICE OF 'A HOUSE FULL OF WOMEN' MAY HOLD THE KEY TO THE IDAHO MURDERS' BIGGEST MYSTERY

Ray has not responded to attempts to reach him or shared details of his recent claims with Fox News Digital.

Ray claimed that the evidence he reviewed shows Kohberger potentially inside the victims’ home, and at other places when they were present prior to the murders — something that both contradicts his own expert report from January 2025 and that even prosecutors haven’t publicly alleged.

"If you look at those precise measurements, there’s probably five that land directly on what would be the living room of the house," Ray told Entin. "Like the latitude-longitude is the physical house itself, and if you put the house back on the map, and you map those, the hits are inside the house."

IDAHO MURDERS: NEW BOOK ON KOHBERGER REVEALS PREVIOUSLY UNSEEN EVIDENCE, CLAIMS SHEATH COULD BE INADMISSIBLE

"I just want to make sure I understand correctly … because I haven't heard this before — so you're saying, based on the data you saw, the latitude-longitude for Bryan Kohberger’s Samsung was in the living room?" Entin asked.

"The AT&T-derived latitude-longitude from the AT&T’s network that it estimates a location, it lands in the house — and it's a 25-meter range, so we're talking 75 feet, so it could be anywhere in the house on any floor," Ray said. "It could technically be outside the house, it could [be] on the property, but it's showing in the immediate area. My personal opinion is when I look at those, and I map what's happening before and after and I'm looking at all the other evidence. I think these are accurate locations."

That runs contrary to the expert report under his name included in a defense filing from Jan. 23, 2025.

SEND US A TIP

"It is my opinion that the geolocation data I have been provided as of the writing this report does not provide any evidence of association between Mr. Kohberger and any of the decedents and/or Mr. Kohberger’s or decedent’s residence," he wrote.

Still, Ray told the podcast his theory is that Mogen was Kohberger’s primary target due to the number of times he could trace their phones to similar locations.

"I believe Maddie was the target," he said, adding that repeated "collisions" between their phones placed them in roughly the same area at the same time, including at a Pullman party the first week of school and at the A&W store near the King Road crime scene.

He also flagged what he described as Kohberger’s broader "pattern of life," pointing to evidence of stalking before the murders.

That also contradicts his report.

GET REAL-TIME UPDATES DIRECTLY ON THE TRUE CRIME HUB

"I am unable to locate any period of time between June 23, 2022 and November 13, 2022 where Mr. Kohberger’s mobile device is in the same specific area as any of the deceased’s mobile devices," he wrote.

The discrepancy raised red flags for some experts who have been following the case, including Morgan Wright, the CEO and founder of the National Center for Open and Unsolved Cases and the host of "Crime: Reconstructed."

That pattern of life was also broken on the night of the murders, when Ray said he believes the plan to target Mogen went awry and resulted in him fleeing south, where he’d never driven before.

While prosecutors alleged that Kohberger had visited the crime scene a dozen times before the murders and at least once the morning after, they have not pointed to "collisions" with any of the victims the way Ray described in the podcast. In a news briefing after Kohberger's guilty plea, the case's lead investigators said they didn't know who the target was.

"The evidence suggested that there was a reason that this particular house was chosen," said then-Moscow Police Cpl. Brett Payne. "What that reason is, we don't know. We don't know who the target was, and we're not going to speculate on that up here today. But we can tell you that, for whatever reason, Mr. Kohberger chose that residence. Perhaps it's the location, layout, we do not know."

And when they were asked by Fox News Digital if they had a motive, lead investigators replied, "We don't."

FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X

On Entin's podcast, Ray alleged that they missed the evidence.

"They didn’t even look at it," Ray said of the stalking evidence. "It’s incredible to me."

SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS

However, in Ray's report, he wrote that he "can find no evidence of stalking behavior or surveillance at the King Road Residence," Wright noted.

"This is the sharpest contradiction," Wright told Fox News Digital. "The state's search warrant sought records specifically to determine whether Kohberger 'stalked' any victim or 'conducted surveillance on the King Road Residence.'"

After Kohberger’s guilty plea, Ray said he offered to do a debrief with the FBI to show the evidence he said he found and they missed. He said he got no response, but added that he has presented before hundreds of law enforcement agencies around the country going back to November, he said.

Last week, Kohberger filed a petition for post-conviction relief, claiming he had ineffective counsel from his defense team.

Ray also speculated that Kohberger’s post-conviction petition was part of a broader legal strategy by his lead defense attorney Anne Taylor despite the plea agreement’s waiver of most appeal rights.

Kohberger pleaded guilty to avoid the death penalty.

"This can never be the standard investigation that we see in cases," Ray said. "This can never be acceptable."

However, he said that he’s confident Kohberger would be convicted anyway at trial — if investigators introduced the evidence he found while working with Taylor.

LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST

"The time is now to start this investigation over," Ray said.

Kohberger had followed other people in the Moscow-Pullman area, he said — a pair of college towns on the border of Washington and Idaho.

"I think he had multiple targets throughout the entire Moscow-Pullman area," Ray said. "Location information and pattern of life is by far the most telling."

Ray said he has no doubt that Kohberger committed the murders.

"If he ever does walk, he will kill again," he said.

item.title: Lifeguards save young boy, 5 years old, as he's pulled unconscious from ocean
item.description: Two lifeguards working at Silver Beach, in Volusia County, Florida, are responsible for rescuing a young child who was pulled unconscious from the ocean during a summer trip.
item.content:encoded:
Another dramatic rescue of a young life has taken place this summer as strong ocean waves and powerful tides continue to prove challenging for vacationers and travelers.

Two lifeguards at Silver Beach in Volusia County, Florida, are being credited with lifesaving action on July 30. 

Lifeguard Dempsey Manhart was just about to take his lunch break, he said, when the family of a young child flagged him down, frantically waving for help, as FOX 35 Orlando reported.

CALIFORNIA LIFEGUARD SPEAKS OUT ON HEARTSTOPPING OCEAN RESCUE: ‘I LOVE WHAT I DO’ 

The boy was unconscious and was being held in the arms of a family member, Manhart recalled. 

He began helping to bring the boy in from the water when his co-lifeguard, Mackenzie Malone, arrived beside him and checked the boy’s pulse — at which point the lifeguards immediately began CPR on the child. 

Malone, who's been working as a lifeguard for her fourth summer, told FOX 35 this was the first time she experienced saving a child from drowning. 

"We’re always expecting anything," she said. "We’re always prepared. We always make sure that we know what to do no matter what the scenario is." 

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

She said the moment her co-lifeguard shouted to her that he was going on a rescue, "I knew that it was going to be serious."

Then everything kicked up a notch. 

"The moment I saw that [the child] was unconscious, that he had a wound on his head … I knew that it was going to be something big." 

The duo began performing CPR on the child.

In short order, he began breathing on his own again. 

Malone later said her lifeguarding and life-saving training kicked in. 

"Thankfully, it ended up in a positive direction," she told FOX 35. "I’m just very grateful that [with] everything we followed, it worked out and that [the boy] actually is able to have a life and come home to a family." 

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

The lifeguards said they hope the rescue of the child provides a reminder for beachgoers to swim near staffed lifeguard towers — where trained responders can provide immediate assistance in an emergency.

"Heroes!! I am grateful to learn just how well-trained beach lifeguards are," wrote a Facebook user about the Florida beach rescue. 

Volusia County is about 50 miles northeast of Orlando, in the east-central region of Florida. 

"God bless their strength," wrote another person. 

The rescue of the 5-year-old boy comes shortly after the heroic rescue of another child, this one by 16-year-old lifeguard Ryder Williams in Santa Cruz, California. Williams braved pounding surf and massive waves to bring a struggling 10-year-old boy safely back to shore, as Fox News Digital reported. 

President Donald J. Trump has invited the teen lifeguard to the White House to celebrate his brave actions. 

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

Fox News Digital previously reported that Los Angeles County lifeguards performed nearly 2,000 ocean rescues during a single weekend this summer as elevated surf and dangerous rip currents swept Southern California beaches. 

Officials have encouraged visitors to speak with lifeguards about ocean conditions before entering the water.

Swimmers caught in a rip current are advised not to fight it. 

Instead, they should remain calm, swim parallel to the shoreline until they escape the current, then angle back toward shore, according to the National Weather Service.

Those who cannot escape should float or tread water and signal for help.

Andrea Margolis of Fox News Digital contributed reporting.

item.title: Princess Margaret, Lord Snowdon's country retreat on the market for first time in history at $5.3 million
item.description: Princess Margaret and Lord Snowdon's former getaway in the countryside is on the market publicly, for the first time in its over 500 year history.
item.content:encoded:
Princess Margaret and Antony Armstrong-Jones, better known as Lord Snowdon's former country retreat, is on the market for the first time in the home's history.

Known as The Old House, the home, which was gifted to Lord Snowdon by his uncle, designer Oliver Messel, prior to his marriage to Princess Margaret, is listed with Blue Book Agency for about $5.3 million.

Originally built in 1481, the cottage in West Sussex came into the possession of the Messel family in 1890 and was passed down for generations before Oliver gifted it to the royal couple.

Upon receiving the 5,750-square-foot home on the 5.52-acre property, Lord Snowdon transformed the dilapidated home into a private retreat away from the public, often hosting many famous faces, including actor Peter Sellers, ballerina Dame Margot Fonteyn, Bianca Jagger, financier Sir Evelyn de Rothschild and more.

PRINCE HARRY AND MEGHAN MARKLE’S $3 MILLION FROGMORE MAKEOVER COULD SOON BE ERASED: EXPERTS

"What Lord Snowdon created here was not simply a private home but an extraordinary creative retreat," Director at Blue Book Agency, Theo James-Wright said. "This was a place where royalty mixed with artists, actors, writers and designers, where some of the most influential figures of the twentieth century gathered behind closed doors. Very few houses can genuinely claim to have witnessed such a remarkable chapter of British cultural history."

The rich history surrounding this house inspired an episode in season three of the popular Netflix series, "The Crown."

Some of the elements Snowdon brought to the home include a redesigned kitchen, a balcony salvaged from Ascot Racecourse's Royal Box during refurbishment works, a lake he created and a "time capsule of royal, cultural and family life" made up of newspaper clippings detailing royal scandals and major events, put together by Snowdon himself.

The estate features a main house with six bedrooms, as well as a pool house which can be used as a guest suite. In addition, the grounds include a garden office, library, tractor shed and other amenities.

While this is the first time the home has been put on the market publicly, Snowdon did sell it privately in 2003, and the current owners purchased it off-market in 2005.

KING CHARLES CONSIDERED QUEEN CAMILLA 'NON-NEGOTIABLE' AFTER PRINCESS DIANA, AUTHOR CLAIMS

"The fact that this is the first time the property has ever been publicly offered for sale makes this a genuinely rare moment," James-Wright said. "Opportunities to acquire houses with this level of provenance, architectural significance and cultural importance simply do not come along very often."

Princess Margaret and Lord Snowdon first met in 1958, and their friendship quickly turned into a romance, with the palace announcing their engagement in February 1960.

They were married just a few months later in May 1960 at Westminster Abbey. Their wedding was the first royal wedding to be televised, attracting an estimated 300 million viewers worldwide.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

Over the course of their marriage, the couple welcomed two children: their son David Armstrong-Jones in November 1961, and their daughter Lady Sarah Chatto in May 1964.

They were married for 16 years before announcing their separation in March 1976, later finalizing their divorce in July 1978. Despite ending their marriage, the two are said to have remained good friends in the following years.

Following their divorce, Lord Snowdon married Lucy Lindsay-Hogg in 1978, while Princess Margaret never remarried.

Princess Margaret died in February 2002 at the age of 71 due to a stroke, after her health began to decline in the 1990s. Lord Snowdon died in January 2017 at the age of 86.

item.title: Why the Orioles at +118 could be the play against Zack Wheeler and the struggling Phillies
item.description: Zack Wheeler takes the mound for the Phillies against Kyle Bradish and the Orioles as both struggling teams battle for wild card positioning.
item.content:encoded:
Well, the trade market is finally coming to a simmer. Perhaps we can call it a boil after yesterday’s blockbuster. We had two major pitchers traded to teams yesterday, with Luis Castillo (in a down year) going from the Mariners to the White Sox, and, of course, Tarik Skubal heading to the Dodgers.

Maybe we should just call the baseball season now and give them their third straight trophy. Two other teams to keep an eye on take each other on today as the Phillies and Orioles square off.

The Philadelphia Phillies are floundering quite a bit. This has been a unique season where we saw them fire their manager after a few weeks of poor play to start the year. That was a move that probably should’ve been done in the offseason anyway. Then they were arguably the best team in baseball for a month or two. Now, they are just five games above .500 and likely going to be wrapped up in a wild card race for the remainder of the season.

The Phillies don’t have a ton of trade resources, but they also don’t need much more than maybe another bat and a better back-end starter. Their front of the rotation is solid with Zack Wheeler and Christopher Sanchez. Wheeler is 10-2 for the season with a 2.53 ERA and a 0.92 WHIP, one of the best pitchers in the game. He did have a couple of tough starts in July, but he also had three quality outings. The Orioles are hitting .250 against Wheeler in 68 at-bats.

The Baltimore Orioles are also struggling, but they’ve pretty much been the same for the entire year. They are three games under .500, but they’ve never seemed to be a team that was going very far.

The thing is, the Orioles have the talent, but some years it just doesn’t click. It appears to be that type of season for Baltimore. Gunner Henderson isn’t having a great season with a .220 average, but he can’t be the sole person to blame for all of this.

I’d point to the pitching and their rotation, as they are really not a very deep squad. They have some good arms, and their bullpen has been much better lately, but they don’t really have a lock-down starter. Maybe the closest is today’s starter, Kyle Bradish. I took him in his last outing, and it was a disaster.

The Tigers jumped on him for 10 hits and five earned runs over 4.2 innings. Phillies hitters have struggled against him over 32 at-bats with a .188 batting average.

Maybe I'm foolish to do this, but I'm going to go against Wheeler. The Orioles are playing slightly better baseball than the Phillies. They both need this game to help with some momentum and to win the series. Wheeler isn't likely to give up a ton of runs, but I think Bradish will bounce back in this outing. The money has come in on the Phillies a bit, but I think that is mostly people just looking at Wheeler and not the full pitcher. Give me the Orioles at +118.

item.title: Kelsey Plum heads to Phoenix Mercury in blockbuster deal hours before WNBA trade deadline
item.description: Kelsey Plum joins the Phoenix Mercury in a blockbuster WNBA trade deadline deal that sent draft picks back to the Los Angeles Sparks late Saturday.
item.content:encoded:
Kelsey Plum is headed to Phoenix.

The Los Angeles Sparks traded the five-time All-Star guard to the Phoenix Mercury late Saturday night in exchange for Monique Akoa Makani, a 2027 first-round pick and a 2028 second-round pick.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

The blockbuster deal came just hours before Sunday afternoon’s WNBA trade deadline and sent the biggest available name on the market to a Mercury team trying to make another postseason run.

Plum, a two-time WNBA champion, has not played since June 21 because of a lower left leg injury. She was expected to return Sunday against the Portland Fire on a minutes restriction, though it is not yet clear whether she will be available when Phoenix visits the Chicago Sky on Monday.

The 31-year-old was putting together one of the best statistical seasons of her career before the injury. Plum is averaging 23.9 points and 6.4 assists through 12 games — both career highs — and led the league in scoring earlier this season.

Her time in Los Angeles lasted only a season and a half.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

The Sparks acquired Plum before the 2025 season in exchange for the No. 2 overall pick, hoping the veteran guard could help accelerate a rebuild centered around Cameron Brink and Rickea Jackson. Seattle eventually used that selection on Dominique Malonga, who became an All-Star in her second season.

But the gamble never produced the turnaround Los Angeles envisioned.

The Sparks missed the playoffs in 2025 and currently sit at 10-17 after losing six straight games. They have gone just 2-9 during Plum’s latest absence and are in danger of missing the postseason for a sixth consecutive year.

MERCURY'S NOW-DELETED SOCIAL MEDIA POST MOCKING CAITLIN CLARK DRAWS SCRUTINY AFTER STAR'S INJURY

Los Angeles also parted ways with general manager Raegan Pebley in July, leaving assistant general managers Zach Knowlton and Nate Nielsen in charge on an interim basis.

Plum was set to become a free agent after the season and reportedly did not plan to re-sign with the Sparks, making her the league’s most prominent trade candidate ahead of the deadline. The New York Liberty and Atlanta Dream had also shown interest.

Instead, she lands with a Phoenix team that appears determined to keep pushing forward despite its own disappointing record. The Mercury are 11-19 and six games behind the eighth-place Liberty for the final playoff spot.

So Plum has her work cut out for her.

She should immediately provide Phoenix with another proven scorer, secondary playmaker and championship-tested guard. She could also take some of the offensive burden away from Alyssa Thomas, who leads the Mercury with 8.3 assists per game.

The move marks only the fourth time in WNBA history that an All-Star has been traded during the season.

item.title: Rubio warns Cuba has infiltrated US with spies, calls communist regime an 'espionage superpower'
item.description: Marco Rubio calls Cuba an "espionage superpower" and claims pro-Hamas, anti-ICE and pro-Maduro protests are linked to a Cuban-hired network.
item.content:encoded:
Secretary of State Marco Rubio raised concerns about Cuba’s ability to infiltrate and influence top-level U.S. institutions, detailing what he described as a dangerous Cuban spy network that is undermining American interests.

"A failed state 90 miles from our shores that happens to be aligned with adversaries to the United States is a national security threat to our country," he told "My View with Lara Trump" on Saturday.

His comments follow the State Department’s recent release of a 100-page report detailing Cuba’s influence operations in the U.S., linking the nation to Antifa and radical activism while labeling it the "capital of 21st-century communism."

CUBA BUILT COVERT NETWORK INSIDE AMERICA THROUGH SPIES, ACTIVISTS AND UNIVERSITIES, STATE DEPT ALLEGES

"They actually are an influence and espionage superpower," Rubio said. "If you look at the history of espionage in the United States, Cuba is the only country that consistently has implanted and embedded spies in our system without even paying them," he said.

"We had… a U.S. ambassador, who ended up being a Cuban spy and was recently convicted," he continued. "We've had them penetrate the highest levels of Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA)."

Former U.S. ambassador and national security official Manuel Rocha pleaded guilty to and was sentenced to 15 years in prison for acting as a secret agent for Cuba for decades.

US COUNTERINTELLIGENCE ‘WAY BEHIND,’ POST-9/11 RECORD ‘EXTRAORDINARILY NEGLIGENT’, FMR TRUMP WH OFFICIAL WARNS

Rubio said Ana Belén Montes, a DIA analyst who was found passing American secrets to Cuba, represents one of the "single biggest intelligence failures" and potentially the most serious penetration in U.S. history.

The secretary also told Fox News that Cuba employs networks of protesters across the country to advocate for different causes in an effort to pressure U.S. lawmakers.

The secretary claimed that pro-Hamas, anti-ICE and pro-Maduro protests are all linked to the same network of Cuban-hired protesters.

"There's nothing organic about it. It is funded, it is organized and Cuba is a part of that network and in some cases a critical part of the network," Rubio said.

US BASES, ICE FACILITIES TARGETED IN CUBA-LINKED 24-HOUR ACTIVIST MOBILIZATION PLAN

"And it's a network they will weaponize against us," he continued. "And they talk about it openly, about how they will use that network to pressure American policymakers."

Rubio also accused Cuba of running dangerous influence campaigns throughout Latin America.

"If you look all throughout Latin America, every communist left-wing insurgency that's destabilized governments across the region, every single one of them over the last 40, 50 years has found its support, its help, in many cases, its birth, from a Cuban influence operation," the secretary said.

Critics of the State Department’s report suggest the report chronicling how Cuba poses a threat to the United States is a scare tactic to potentially justify U.S. military action against the country.

Rubio dismissed Americans who sympathize with Cuba’s one-party communist republic led by President Miguel Díaz-Canel.

"I know there are plenty of people in American academia and, frankly, in American press that sympathize with the Cuban regime and have for a very long time," he said. "Part of it is motivated by their anti-Americanism and part of it motivated by ideological affinity."

"But it doesn't mean we can ignore this threat," he warned.

item.title: GOP Rep Max Miller pushes back against abuse allegations: ‘I have nothing to hide’
item.description: Ohio Rep. Max Miller went live on X Sunday morning to address and deny allegations made by his ex-wife that he previously abused her and their daughter.
item.content:encoded:
Rep. Max Miller, R-Ohio, went live on X Sunday morning, denying allegations from his ex-wife that he abused her and their daughter.

"I'm not getting out of this race, and I'm winning in November," Miller said at the end of an X livestream statement with pictures of his family in the background.

Miller said his ex-wife, Emily Moreno, the daughter of Sen. Bernie Moreno, R-Ohio, has documented mental health circumstances that might have led to her allegations after their public divorce. 

"They frame me as an abuser," Miller said, saying there is "no evidence" against him.

"No court or agency has even substantiated any allegation against me," he added. "Every single one of these allegations were already investigated."

Miller released troves of evidence via Dropbox that he says undermines the allegations against him.

"I have nothing to hide," he said.

Faced with a narrow path to winning control of the U.S. House, Democrats are seeing fresh opportunity in a northeast Ohio congressional seat where the Republican incumbent is facing mounting pressure over allegations that he abused his ex-wife and daughter in a bitter and drawn-out dispute with his former spouse.

Allegations against Miller, a White House adviser during President Donald Trump's first term, have been public for years but have recently drawn increased media scrutiny amid an escalating legal back-and-forth with his ex-wife. That has Democrats sensing Miller could be vulnerable in a district he won two years ago with just over 51% of the vote.

Over the past week, they have called for Miller to resign, requested a congressional ethics investigation and suggested more help could be directed in the fall toward his Democratic opponent, union ironworker Brian Poindexter. item.title: Buffalo Bills moved on from Sean McDermott but their offseason moves won't be enough for a title
item.description: The Buffalo Bills hired Joe Brady and added DJ Moore and Bradley Chubb, but questions remain about whether Josh Allen can finally reach the Super Bowl.
item.content:encoded:
At what point do you give up on a team? When do you say "enough is enough" and make the decision to just believe it won’t happen for a squad?

I’m at that point personally, as I can’t support the Buffalo Bills winning a Super Bowl anymore. Last season had virtually everything break correctly for them, and they couldn’t get it done, so why do we think they will this year?

As mentioned, they didn’t win the Super Bowl, and they actually lost a playoff game in yet another heartbreaking fashion. The regular season was… odd. They started with four straight wins and looked dominant. They came back in a thriller to open the year and win 41-40 over the Ravens. Then they lost back-to-back weeks to the Patriots (who turned out to be very good) and the terrible Falcons. Their other losses came against the Dolphins, Texans, and Eagles. The Dolphins and Falcons were the only two-score losses they had during the year. They struggled to beat the Jaguars, then lost in overtime to the Broncos.

JOSH ALLEN RECALLS HIS ROLE IN BILLS' COACHING SEARCH, DETAILS JOE BRADY’S APPROACH TO NEW ROLE

I think the team also said they’ve had enough as they finally moved on from Sean McDermott. I don’t think you can really blame McDermott for everything, but sometimes you do need to switch it up and get rid of the coach. They hired Joe Brady, who is more offense-focused, and I’m not sure that was their major problem. They added DJ Moore to the team, and he might have his best seasons behind him. They added another guy who might have his best behind him in Bradley Chubb as well.

JOSH ALLEN SAYS HE WOULD BE 'VERY HONORED' TO PLAY FOR TEAM USA IN FLAG FOOTBALL AT 2028 OLYMPICS

A team that probably could use help on defense doesn’t seem to have done much to address the issue. The best defense for the team is keeping Josh Allen on the field, I guess. Allen is still elite and will keep the Bills relevant no matter what the rest of their unit looks like. It just feels like this team is being pieced together with randomness instead of a full plan. I want to see them start making moves that will push them ahead, not just keep them winning double-digits and relying on luck and Allen’s magic in the postseason.

I think the Patriots take a bit of a step back, as mentioned, but I really don’t see that happening with Allen under center for the Bills. They still have a tough schedule, but 10 wins does feel like the floor for this team every year, right? They’ve had 11 wins or more every year since 2020. I don’t see that changing here. I think a fun bet for them this year is over 4.5 division wins. I think they split with the Patriots, and they should sweep the Jets and Dolphins which gives you five wins. Since 2020, they have gotten five or more division wins three times. It is +115, so I like that look for them as well.

item.title: 'Remember the Titans' star Ethan Suplee issues warning about weight-loss drug craze
item.description: Ethan Suplee warns GLP-1 weight-loss drugs aren't a "one-stop shop," saying resistance training and healthy habits are essential for lasting results.
item.content:encoded:
Ethan Suplee pumped the brakes on the GLP-1 craze, warning that the wildly popular weight-loss drugs aren't the miracle fix many people believe they are.

As millions of Americans continue turning to blockbuster GLP-1 medications, Suplee said the drugs are only one piece of the puzzle. Drawing from his own decades-long weight-loss journey, the actor said sustainable success comes from building healthier habits instead of relying on medication alone.

Suplee has been candid about his decades-long battle with obesity. The "Remember the Titans" actor weighed roughly 500 pounds at his heaviest and ultimately lost around 300 pounds through years of diet and lifestyle changes. He has also undergone multiple skin-removal surgeries and now hosts weekly discussions on his show, "LifeLONG with Ethan Suplee," about long-term weight management.

MAYIM BIALIK DETAILS 'NIGHTMARE' AFTER ONE INJECTION OF GLP-1 DRUG LED TO WEEKS OF DEBILITATING SIDE EFFECTS

The 50-year-old actor started dieting at just 5 years old and later, by his own volition, at age 24. "And I kind of spun my wheels for 15 years on these yo-yo diets simply because I didn't communicate," Suplee told Fox News Digital. "And when I didn't communicate to anyone else, I didn't actually figure out what I really wanted."

After decades of trial and error, Suplee said his own experience taught him there isn't a shortcut to lasting weight loss. While he acknowledged the weight-loss drugs can be an effective tool, he argued they aren't a replacement for building healthier habits.

"As a kid, I wanted a magical diet drug so badly. And now we have what is a magical diet drug," he said. "I think, unfortunately, it's also not a one-stop shop. I think you can hop on a GLP-1 and experience weight loss. You can see the scale go down week over week for a long time without having to do anything else."

"... I think when people imagine their ideal — I don't think the GLP-1s get anyone to their ideal."

'REMEMBER THE TITANS' STAR ETHAN SUPLEE SHOWS OFF MUSCLES AFTER DRASTIC WEIGHT LOSS TRANSFORMATION

Suplee emphasized that the medications can dramatically improve people's health and said he wouldn't discourage anyone from using them.

"By the way, a small amount of weight loss provides a huge health benefit," he added. "So if you're just going into it, going like, 'I just want to be healthier. Let me hop on this GLP-1 agonist and improve my health.' Bravo to you. You're going to do that... I'm not criticizing those people."

But Suplee said the conversation becomes more nuanced for people hoping to reach an "ideal" weight or transform their physique.

"I think for those people, just hopping on a GLP-1 is not enough," Suplee added. "I think it also will require some resistance training to preserve lean tissue... maybe increase protein a bit... I just think [they] aren't a one-stop shop."

WATCH: ‘REMEMBER THE TITANS’ STAR ETHAN SUPLEE WARNS POPULAR GLP-1 DRUGS AREN'T A CURE-ALL FOR LASTING WEIGHT LOSS

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

The "My Name is Earl" star said his own experience ultimately shaped a simple philosophy: There's no single answer when it comes to long-term weight loss. He said lasting success comes from addressing the many factors that influence a person's health and relationship with food.

"I don't think it's ever going to be one thing," Suplee explained. "I think it is partially the amount of food you're consuming, partially the types of food you're consuming, partially how sedentary you are, and partially your emotional and potentially mental behavior and relationship with food."

"There's an ecosystem to everybody's life."

It's a lesson Suplee said became even clearer after he reached his goal weight.

"I found maintaining weight loss to be a hell of a lot harder and more complicated than losing weight," he admitted.

Suplee said he still grapples with the same cravings he experienced before losing roughly 300 pounds.

"If I see an advertisement for McDonald's, I want McDonald's," he said. "I'm hungry. This is true today as it was 20 years ago."

WATCH: ETHAN SUPLEE SAYS WEIGHT LOSS WOULD BRING NEW EDGE TO ROLE HE'D LOVE TO REVISIT

He was quick to clarify that long-term weight maintenance isn't about completely cutting out fast food, including McDonald's.

"But it's not eating it emotionally, not eating it to cure my anxiety, not eating it out of compulsion, and then not overeating it," Suplee added. "Like, these are all the factors I have to deal with to maintain my weight."

When asked what has allowed him to maintain his weight loss over the years, Suplee pointed to a less obvious factor: learning to be honest with himself by opening up to others.

"I found I could become more honest with myself by opening up and being honest with other people," Suplee said. "And I think that really made a huge difference in my ability to maintain this weight loss as long as I have."

item.title: Ancient Book of Revelation city gives up stunning secret buried for 1,500 years
item.description: A 1,500-year-old geometric mosaic with a heart-shaped ivy leaf was uncovered in ancient Smyrna, one of the seven churches in the Book of Revelation.
item.content:encoded:
An ancient mosaic was recently revealed in a Turkish city long known for being one of the seven churches mentioned in the Book of Revelation.

The artwork was uncovered in the ancient city of Smyrna, an archaeological site in modern-day İzmir, Turkey, according to Turkish state news outlet Anadolu Agency (AA).

Smyrna — along with Ephesus, Pergamum, Thyatira, Sardis, Philadelphia and Laodicea — is one of the seven churches of Asia Minor addressed by Jesus in the Book of Revelation.

ARCHAEOLOGISTS UNEARTH ANCIENT TREASURE CACHE AT BIBLICAL CITY CONNECTED TO GENESIS

Revelation 2:8 states: "To the angel of the church in Smyrna write: These are the words of him who is the First and the Last, who died and came to life again."

The mosaic was found during infrastructure work at the archaeological site. It dates to between the fourth and sixth centuries A.D., according to officials, and measures roughly 16.4 by 8.2 feet.

Photos show archaeologists brushing away centuries of dirt to reveal the remarkably preserved 1,500-year-old mosaic and its geometric and floral motifs.

Excavation director Akın Ersoy said the mosaic was first found last year, but archaeologists did not fully excavate the artwork until this year, according to AA.

LOST SERMONS FROM ONE OF CHRISTIANITY'S GREATEST SAINTS DISCOVERED AFTER 1,600 YEARS

"In connection with this, we also found traces of the walls that defined the space," said Ersoy.

"We believe that a structure was built over the mosaic during the Ottoman period in the 19th century, and that the new layout was created while avoiding damage to the mosaic floor as much as possible."

The most striking motif is the heart-shaped ivy leaf, which is made of red tesserae, or mosaic tiles.

Though modern people see the heart as a symbol of love, Ersoy said the mosaic was created long before the symbol came to represent romance.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

"It was not very clear in the early periods that the heart represented affection and love. We see the heart emerge as a symbol of love in paintings during the Renaissance," he said.

Rather, Ersoy said the heart-shaped ivy leaf was intended to symbolize loyalty.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

"The ivy leaf clings to trees and walls," he said. "It came to symbolize loyalty and has been used from antiquity through the centuries."

Archaeologists also uncovered bags, cooking pots and earthenware vessels dating to the late Ottoman Empire and the early years of the Turkish Republic, suggesting the space was reused roughly 1,500 years after the mosaic was laid.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"We can say that the people of that period consciously protected it because there is very little damage," the archaeologist said.

"The space was brought back to life after 1,500 years."

The latest discovery is one of several recent archaeological finds in cities mentioned in the Book of Revelation.

Last summer, archaeologists uncovered a massive Roman council hall in Laodicea, which featured carvings linked to early Christian worship.

Months later, archaeologists announced the discovery of a Roman-era marble bathtub and other ancient artifacts in Ephesus.

item.title: Southern university requires business suits, bans du-rags and other headwear in new dress code
item.description: Tuskegee University's new dress code bans du-rags, bonnets and sagging pants in classrooms as part of its broader workforce readiness push.
item.content:encoded:
Retired U.S. Air Force Maj. Gen. Dr. Mark Brown, president and CEO of Tuskegee University in Alabama, is bringing forward a "professional educational environment" to one of the nation's most prestigious Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCU).

Students will be required to bring a business suit and shoes to campus for business-like meetings and cannot dress unprofessionally in the classrooms or cafeterias. Head coverings will also be barred, with exceptions for those that serve religious or medical purposes.

"The university has developed a new policy for student attire on campus, classroom attendance, and cell phone use in classrooms," Brown wrote in a message to students. "Tuskegee students now have a dress code for public and professional places."

"The Student Handbook requires students to arrive on campus with a business suit and proper shoes for a business meeting," the message said. "Students are prohibited from wearing revealing clothing in class, to the cafeteria or in official settings like Convocation. They are also not able to wear bedroom shoes, bonnets, or du-rags to class or the cafeteria."

MICHELLE OBAMA ACCUSES MEDIA OF WEAPONIZING FASHION TO 'DIMINISH' HER AS A CAMPAIGN THREAT

The Alabama school is also restricting revealing and sexually explicit clothing as part of a broader push to prepare college students for the workforce.

"The goal here is not meant to restrict you from enjoying the Tuskegee Experience, but to prepare you with a solid foundation for the workforce you will enter once you leave Tuskegee," Brown, who took over as Tuskegee University president two years ago, wrote. "Employers are less forgiving and too often presentation may overrule stellar preparation.

"Tuskegee University continues to prepare the best and brightest for a lifetime of success," Brown added. "With these changes, we want to ensure every student is as prepared as they can be. I look forward to seeing you in August."

STUDENT LOAN RULE WOULD PENALIZE GRADUATES WHO ENTER MINISTRY, CHRISTIAN COLLEGE LEADERS SAY

Tuskegee’s fall orientation guidance lists business attire for career fairs, meetings, interviews and other professional occasions, but the guidance does restrict unprofessional attire in classrooms, too.

"Hats, bonnets, head scarves, caps, hoods, du-rags, bandanas, sunglasses, and other non-religious or non-medically required head coverings should be removed while in the classroom or cafeteria unless they are required for documented medical, religious, cultural, or University-approved purposes," the Dress Code Policy for Students that accompanied Brown's message read.

"Pants, skirts, dresses, and shorts should be worn in a manner that is appropriate for a professional educational environment. Clothing should fit properly and not expose undergarments or other private areas. Excessively short shorts, swimsuit bottoms, body suits, sleeveless undershirts, and similar casual garments are not appropriate for professional classroom settings," the guidance continued. "T-shirts worn as dresses and sagging pants are not permitted. Baggy or loose fitting pants must be worn with a belt that fits around the waist."

UNITED PASSENGER SAYS CREW ORDERED HIM TO CHANGE CONTROVERSIAL T-SHIRT BEFORE HE COULD TRAVEL

Faculty members will be authorized to respond when students are dressed in violation of the guidelines, though the president’s message did not specify potential penalties.

Some elements of the announcement reinforce standards that were already on the books. Tuskegee’s 2025-26 student handbook required students to dress "in good taste," prohibited sleepwear outside residence halls and barred men from wearing "do rags," stocking caps, bandanas, baseball caps and other headwear inside university buildings. It also prohibited sagging pants in academic facilities.

The revised rules have fueled a wider debate over professionalism, cultural expression and the expectations placed on students at HBCUs. Critics online have described restrictions on du-rags and bonnets as respectability politics that unfairly target clothing associated with Black culture.

Supporters argue that colleges should teach students how to present themselves during interviews, meetings and other professional situations.

Several alumni have defended the university’s approach. Tuskegee graduate Gwen McKinney told NBC4 Washington that the policy was "a breath of fresh air," saying there is "a time and place and a setting for every kind of dress."

"A critical part of being ready for and confident in business environments is being appropriately dressed," Walter P. Cooper Sr., director of the Career Education and Leadership Development Center, said.

"We know that every workplace doesn’t require business attire – our center includes business casual and casual attire, too – but as our students prepare to enter those workplace scenarios that do, it is important that access to the right wardrobe is not a barrier."

For students that might not have the proper attire, there is The Golden Tigers Community Closet to help outfit needy students.

"One of the key pillars of Tuskegee’s Renaissance Era is our focus on career readiness for our students," Brown said. "Academically, we are equipping our students to stand shoulder to shoulder with any candidates competing for roles in the global economy.

"The Golden Tigers Community Closet is an important way to ensure that every student can also feel confidently dressed when they step into those spaces."

The dress code is part of a larger set of classroom and career-readiness rules being introduced as Tuskegee expects its highest new-student enrollment in 32 years. Cellphone use will be prohibited unless authorized by an instructor.

"Faculty will be empowered to respond to students who are inappropriately dressed based on these guidelines," Brown's message to students added.

"Faculty will also be able to respond to a different classroom challenge – cell phones. Unless directed by the professor, students are no longer allowed to use their cell phones while in class. They should be turned off to eliminate any distraction from the instructor’s lesson."

Fox News Digital reached out to Brown's office and the university for further comment. VP of stragetic communications Thonnia Lee confirmed the details of the president's message to students and the dress code but declined further comment.

item.title: Mackenzie Phillips says 'morals clause' led to abrupt exit from 'One Day at a Time'
item.description: Mackenzie Phillips reveals the lunch break confrontation that triggered her "morals clause" and ended her role on "One Day at a Time" in 1980.
item.content:encoded:
Mackenzie Phillips is reflecting on the moment that ended her run on "One Day at a Time."

The sitcom star recently attended Fanboy Expo Knoxville in Tennessee, where she spoke about the "morals clause" in her contract and how it contributed to her abrupt departure from the series.

"One Day at a Time" made Phillips a household name alongside co-stars Bonnie Franklin and Valerie Bertinelli. Behind the scenes, however, the actress was battling addiction. The 66-year-old said her struggles with substance abuse led to additional provisions in her contract.

MACKENZIE PHILLIPS SAYS SHE AND VALERIE BERTINELLI DRANK WINE, DID COCAINE DURING SITCOM BREAKS

"We all had a morals contract, but mine was a little more specific," she said at the event, People magazine reported.

According to the outlet, the actress said that if producers suspected she was "under the influence," they would "have the right to take [me] to a doctor for urinalysis."

Phillips said everything changed during a lunch break between scenes.

WATCH: MACKENZIE PHILLIPS REVEALS WILD COCAINE-FILLED BREAKS WITH VALERIE BERTINELLI

"One day, I was asleep on the couch," she recalled. "It was lunch hour. Everybody would just take a little nap. And [co-executive producer] Patricia Fass Palmer, who I hated for years, and now we're very good friends, she came up to me, and she said, 'Mac, wake up. Wake up. We're gonna take you to the doctor and have you pee in a cup.'"

Phillips told the panel her first reaction was to ask for more time, knowing that "cocaine runs through your system so quickly." Palmer, however, immediately shut down the idea.

Palmer then told her it was time to leave.

"She said, 'No, we're not waiting until tomorrow,'" Phillips said. "And I said, 'OK, well.' She said, 'All right, Mac. Grab your stuff and get it together. Get all your stuff. And leave.' So that's what I did. And that was that."

Phillips starred in "One Day at a Time" from 1975 to 1980 before her character was written off following her firing, according to People. She later returned for a guest arc before leaving the series for good in 1983, the outlet reported.

Phillips has continued to speak candidly about her struggles with addiction in recent interviews.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

Back in May, Phillips told Fox News Digital that one memory from her time on the show might still surprise fans today.

"Oh, I don't know. Oh, OK. So, this might surprise you — during lunch break, Valerie and I would drive to my house, get in the pool, drink wine and snort coke," Phillips said.

Phillips quickly clarified that Bertinelli has also spoken openly about that period.

"Valerie talks about it openly, so it's not like I'm pulling her covers or anything," she said. "... Valerie didn't have the kind of addiction that I had; she didn't have addiction."

The former child star said drug use was also common behind the scenes of the sitcom.

"And you know, so we would do coke together in the dressing room and stuff," Phillips said.

LIKE WHAT YOU’RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

"I just happened to be the one that got caught. And thank God I got caught, you know?"

Asked by Fox News Digital what keeps her grounded today, Phillips pointed to her faith and perspective.

"What keeps me grounded is my faith and just knowing how strong and… empowered my history has made me," Phillips said.

She said people sometimes respond to her life story with pity, but that's not how she sees it.

"Someone was just saying, 'Oh my God, I feel so sorry for everything you went through,'" Phillips recalled. "And I was like, 'Don't feel sorry for me because everything I went through, even though it was horrible and difficult, made me the woman I am today.'"

WATCH: MACKENZIE PHILLIPS SAYS FAITH AND RESILIENCE HELPED SHAPE WHO SHE IS TODAY

Phillips said she does not believe she could erase parts of her past and remain the same person.

"If I could go back and just take this part out, then I might not be who I am," she said. "And I feel very blessed in my life."

The actress has been candid for years about addiction, trauma and recovery. Phillips is the daughter of John Phillips, co-founder of The Mamas & the Papas, and his first wife, Susan Adams. She chronicled her life in her memoir "High on Arrival" and later explored recovery in "Hopeful Healing."

During her conversation with Fox News Digital, Phillips said resilience has become central to how she views her life.

"I have a high, high resilience," she said. "You know, the love of my son, my family, my sisters — even though that relationship was very difficult for a long time — I just believe ... I have a strong faith, and, I mean, I had no choice. Be resilient or die."

Phillips has also used her recovery to help others. In addition to acting, she has worked in the addiction and recovery field, including as a counselor and manager at Breathe Life Healing Centers.
